topicName: Lumen Global Illumination and Reflections Setup
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: Setting Up Lumen Global Illumination and Reflections in Unreal Engine"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Lumen is Unreal Engine's fully dynamic global illumination and reflections system. Designed for next-generation games and real-time visualization, Lumen reacts immediately to direct lighting and geometry changes, removing the need for pre-computed lightmaps."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Project Settings Configuration"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before enabling Lumen in your level, you must configure your project settings to ensure the rendering pipeline supports hardware ray tracing and dynamic GI."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Open Project Settings via Edit > Project Settings."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Navigate to Engine > Rendering."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Locate the Global Illumination section and ensure Lumen is set as the default."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Locate the Reflections section and set the Reflection Method to Lumen."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Under Hardware Ray Tracing, check \"Support Hardware Ray Tracing\" if your target platform supports it for higher fidelity."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Configuring Post Process Volume"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Lumen is controlled globally via a Post Process Volume. If you do not have one in your scene, you need to spawn and configure it."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Place a Post Process Volume from the Place Actors panel into your level."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In the Details panel, check \"Infinite Extent (Unbound)\" so it affects the entire world."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scroll down to the Lumen Global Illumination settings."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Set Dynamic Global Illumination Method to Lumen."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Fine-Tuning Lumen Reflections"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Lumen reflections provide accurate specular reflections with multiple bounces. You can optimize quality and performance inside the Post Process Volume."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Locate the Lumen Reflections section in the Post Process Volume."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Adjust \"Max Roughness to Reflect\" to balance performance and visual quality on rough surfaces."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Increase \"Reflection Detail\" if you require sharper reflections on intricate meshes."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Debugging and Performance Optimization"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"To diagnose Lumen performance issues or light leaking, use the built-in Unreal Engine visualization modes."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"Console Command: ViewMode LumenScene"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Use the 'LumenScene' view mode to inspect the simplified geometry that Lumen uses for ray tracing. Ensure your meshes are generating proper signed distance fields (SDFs)."}]
